data.message: Heading to upper engine, come with me!

I found Diana's body in upper engine just now. My route was cafeteria → oxygen → upper engine. I was with Eve in oxygen from tick 4 through 6 — she came in from upper engine right when I arrived. When I got to upper engine at tick 7, Bob was there standing over Diana's body.

So Bob and Eve are my main suspects. Eve came from upper engine right before I got to oxygen — she could've killed Diana and fled. Bob was literally in the room with the body when I arrived. I want to hear both of their routes carefully.

I was on the east side the whole round. My route was security → weapons → security. I saw Alice in weapons at ticks 4 and 5 — she was there doing what looked like a task. I came back to security after that. I never went anywhere near upper engine, oxygen, or cafeteria, so I can't speak directly to what happened with Diana.

Frank's info is the key here — Bob standing over the body is very suspicious, but Eve coming out of upper engine right before is also a strong lead. I want to hear Bob and Eve explain their routes before I commit to a vote. Alice is essentially cleared in my book unless someone contradicts me.

I can confirm Charlie's account — my route was navigation → security → weapons, and I saw Charlie in weapons at ticks 4 and 5. We were together on the east side of the map, nowhere near upper engine. So Charlie and I can vouch for each other.

That means the killer is among Bob, Eve, or Frank. Frank's story puts suspicion on both Bob and Eve, but I want to think about this carefully. Frank claims Eve came into oxygen from upper engine at tick 4 — if that's true, Eve had opportunity. But Frank himself ended up in upper engine with the body, and reporters can sometimes be the killer trying to control the narrative.

Bob being "over the body" is suspicious on its face, but if Bob just walked in and found her, that's exactly what an innocent discoverer looks like too — Frank just beat him to the report button.

I really need to hear Bob and Eve's routes before voting. Right now Eve is my lean suspect because Frank's timing on her coming from upper engine is the most concrete lead, but I'm not locked in.

Okay, let me clear up Frank's timeline because he's got it slightly off in a way that matters.

My route was upper engine → oxygen. I was in upper engine at the very start, then moved to oxygen. Frank arrived in oxygen at tick 5 — I was already there or arrived right around the same time, and we were together in oxygen at ticks 5 and 6. So Frank and I can vouch for each other being in oxygen during that window.

Here's the important part: when I left upper engine, Diana was NOT dead. I didn't see a body there. That means she was killed AFTER I left — which means either Bob killed her when he got there, or Frank killed her when HE got to upper engine at tick 7 and immediately "reported" to control the narrative.

Frank's framing of me is suspicious. Yes, I came from upper engine — but he knows I was with him in oxygen for two full ticks, which is a solid alibi. Pushing me as a "main suspect" feels like deflection.

So it's Bob or Frank. Bob being in the room with the body is the classic discoverer scenario — but so is Frank reporting it. I want to hear Bob's route. If Bob came from somewhere that gave him time to kill Diana between when I left and when Frank arrived, he's the killer. If Bob just arrived at tick 7 same as Frank, then Frank is our duck.

Bob, you're last — your route matters a lot here.

My route was electrical → medbay → upper engine. I was doing electrical first, then I went through medbay and saw Diana alive there earlier. I headed up to upper engine for the align engine task, and when I got there the body was basically right there — Frank came in and reported before I even had time to react.

I get why it looks bad that I was in the room, but I did not kill Diana. I wasn’t “standing over it” waiting around, I had just arrived from medbay side.

The thing that bothers me is Frank’s story: he’s saying Eve is a main suspect, but also says he was with Eve in oxygen for multiple ticks. That feels like he’s trying to keep both me and Eve available as suspects instead of committing. If Eve was really with him in oxygen, then this is probably a Frank self-report or he walked in at the exact same time as me.

From my perspective, vote is Frank over Eve. He reported instantly and shaped the whole narrative around me being there.

I want to clarify and push back on a few things.

First, Eve — yes, you were with me in oxygen ticks 4-6, that's a solid alibi for that window. I'm not married to you being the killer. I flagged you initially because you came FROM upper engine at tick 4, which is where Diana died. But if Diana was alive when you left, that points elsewhere.

Bob — your route is electrical → medbay → upper engine. That's a long path. Electrical to medbay is one move, medbay to upper engine is another. You'd arrive at upper engine around tick 5-6, not tick 7. That gives you time alone with Diana before I arrived. When I walked in at tick 7, you were right next to the body — not "just arriving."

To Bob's accusation that I'm self-reporting: if I killed Diana, why would I immediately report and put myself in the room? Eve vouches I was in oxygen ticks 4-6. The kill happened between Eve leaving upper engine and my arrival at tick 7 — and Bob is the only person we know was in upper engine during that window.

My vote is leaning Bob. But I want to hear if anyone can verify Bob's medbay claim.

Okay, going second round so I'll share what I've taken in.

Alice and I confirm each other on the east side — neither of us is the killer. That leaves Bob, Eve, and Frank.

Eve and Frank vouch for each other in oxygen ticks 5-6, which is a mutual alibi. That's either both clean or both ducks working together — but in a 1-duck game, mutual alibis usually mean both clean.

So the math points to Bob. And Frank's timing point is sharp: electrical → medbay → upper engine should put Bob in upper engine before tick 7, giving him alone-time with Diana after Eve left. Bob saying he "just arrived" the same tick as Frank doesn't match the travel times.

The one thing that could flip this: nobody can verify Bob was actually in medbay or electrical. If someone saw him there, I'd reconsider. Otherwise I'm leaning Bob.

Diana's dead so she can't confirm seeing Bob in medbay either — convenient for him.

I'm leaning Bob but want to hear if Diana was seen by anyone else earlier.

This is my second speech, and Charlie laid it out well so I'll build on it.

The mutual alibi between Eve and Frank in oxygen ticks 5-6 is the key piece. In a 1-duck game, that means both are almost certainly clean — a duck wouldn't fabricate an alibi with an innocent because the innocent would contradict them.

That leaves Bob. And Frank's travel-time math is the nail: electrical → medbay → upper engine is two moves. If Bob left electrical at tick 4, he'd be in medbay by tick 5 and upper engine by tick 6 at the earliest — giving him a full tick alone with Diana before Frank arrived at tick 7. His claim that he "just arrived" the same time as Frank doesn't add up to the travel distances.

Nobody can verify Bob in medbay or electrical. Diana might have been the one to see him there, and she's conveniently dead.

I'm voting Bob.

Alice and Charlie have laid this out clearly, and I agree with their reasoning.

To reinforce: I was in upper engine at the start and Diana was alive when I left. I moved to oxygen and was with Frank there at ticks 5 and 6 — that's a solid mutual alibi. In a 1-duck game, mutual alibis between two players almost always mean both are clean, because a duck wouldn't risk fabricating one with an innocent who could contradict them.

That leaves Bob. And Frank's travel math is correct — electrical → medbay → upper engine puts Bob in upper engine by tick 5 or 6, not tick 7. He had the window alone with Diana after I left. His "just arrived same time as Frank" story doesn't match the distances.

Nobody can verify his medbay or electrical claims, and Diana — the one person who might have — is dead.

I'm voting Bob.

Hold on — everyone is applying travel-time math to me but not to Frank, and that’s the part that doesn’t add up.

Frank and Eve are both saying they were together in oxygen through tick 6. Oxygen to upper engine is not instant — if Frank was genuinely still in oxygen at tick 6, how is he in upper engine reporting at tick 7? Either the oxygen alibi timing is wrong, or Frank’s route/timing is wrong.

My actual point is: I saw Diana alive earlier in medbay, and she headed toward upper engine. When I got to upper engine, I was going to the align engine task. I did not kill her. Frank came in and immediately reported, then framed it as me “standing over the body,” which is an easy way to make the first person he sees look guilty.

Eve leaving upper early doesn’t clear Frank for what happened after. The kill window is late, and Frank is the one controlling the report and the narrative. If we’re voting on timing inconsistencies, Frank’s oxygen-to-upper timing is the biggest one here.

I’m voting Frank.
